item.title: Vietjet next to land at Western Sydney International Airport
item.content:
Direct flights from Western Sydney to South East Asia are on the way, with Vietjet signing on to fly from the Western Sydney International (Nancy-Bird Walton) Airport (WSI).

Taking off in January 2027, Vietjet will operate twice weekly to Ho Chi Minh City, increasing to three times weekly in March. The new services will be operated by Vietjet’s A330 fleet, with each plane carrying up to 377 passengers.

From November 2027, Vietjet Thailand plans to start fourweekly services from Badgerys Creek to Bangkok. The new services are subject to regulatory approvals.

The announcement was welcomed in Sydney today by General Secretary and President of the Socialist Republic of Vietnam To Lam, and Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade, Matt Thistlethwaite.

Vietjet is the fifth airline to announce flights in and out of Western Sydney International Airport, joining Jetstar, Air New Zealand, Singapore Airlines and Qantas.

Vietjet’s new flights to Ho Chi Minh City are supported by the NSW Government’s Take-Off Fund.

Western Sydney’s new 24-hour airport is the centrepiece of the Albanese Labor Government's near $18 billion investment in Western Sydney, including the future Sydney Metro Airport rail connection and significant road upgrades to nearby Elizabeth Drive, Fifteenth Avenue and Mamre Road. This investment builds upon benefits already delivered through the recent opening of the M12 Motorway.

Quotes attributable to Prime Minister Anthony Albanese:

“Western Sydney deserves an airport with global connections, and that’s exactly what we’re delivering.

“As we welcome the General Secretary and President of Vietnam To Lam to Australia, it’s great to see our growing partnership delivering practical benefits.

“These new direct flights will bring our people closer together, boost tourism and trade, and create new opportunities for Western Sydney.”

Quotes attributable to Federal Minister for Infrastructure, Transport, Regional Development and Local Government Catherine King:

“This is Vietjet’s fifth Australian destination, and a sign of the momentum we’re seeing build at Sydney’s newest airport.

“With just 76 days until passenger flights begin at Western Sydney International Airport, testing at the terminal, fit out and final touches are underway to get it ready to welcome the new passengers.

“It’s an exciting few months ahead for Western Sydney and their new airport.”

Quotes attributable to NSW Tourism Minister Steve Kamper:

“Western Sydney International Airport is getting ready for take-off, and the Minns Labor Government is proud to support the flights from Western Sydney to Vietnam through the Western Sydney International Take-Off Fund.

“With the new airport getting closer to opening for passenger flights, this is an incredibly exciting time for local tourism, businesses and jobs.”

Quotes attributable to Assistant Minister for Foreign Affairs and Trade Matt Thistlethwaite:

“Australia and Vietnam continue to build a partnership grounded in shared prosperity and deepening people‑to‑people links.

“Vietjet’s new services strengthen that relationship by creating more opportunities for travel, trade and connection between our two nations.”
